title: Northline AE Calibration

brief.summary: A dedicated hunter in London winning net-new mid-market and enterprise customers for Northline's CRM, across B2B SaaS companies and e-commerce brands.
must_haves: 2+ years closing technical SaaS, full cycle
Wins net-new customers and beats target, repeatably
Strong discovery on complex or unclear needs
brief.level: Mid-level closer. Pure new business, no farming.

questions: If you can't have both CRM category experience and new business wins in one of our target verticals, which matters more?
Which vertical should this hire make progress in first: B2B SaaS or e-commerce?
Enterprise closer from day one, or a strong mid-market closer who grows into enterprise?
How much pipeline must this person generate alone? Would you hire someone who has never self-sourced most of it?
method:
The candidate types come from the Northline brief and research into how comparable new business AE roles are advertised and staffed in London: job ads from CRM vendors and e-commerce and revenue-tech SaaS companies, recruiter ads for mid-market and enterprise AE roles, and commentary on how AI is changing the AE role in 2026.

The six profiles were found with Clay's public professional data, searching current London-based staff at each type's typical employers by title. They were matched on current title, employer and location only. Their closing record and suitability have not been checked, and nobody has been contacted. Three are close to the brief, two are borderline (close, but missing one thing the brief asks for), and one is an edge case from a different background that would widen the search if the team likes it.
